Picasso Toys Magnetic Drawing Board 12x10 inch Large 748 Bead Magnet Tablet Pad Erasable Reusable Writing Playboard STEM Toys Educational Playset Open-Ended Learning Kit Child Brain Development PTB01 In concept, great. I do think, if used as intended, it helps work their prancer grip muscles, which need to be built up in preparation for writing. Unfortunately, either the size of the letters are too small and/or the size of the magnetic balls are too big, because when you run the 'pen' over the letters, they don't pull up the balls in the way/order they should (some balls that I want to pull up later come up already, and some of the balls fall back down). Also because of how large the balls are, it is difficult to actually 'draw' something recognizable on the flip side.

I thought my kids (3 and 5) would love this product, and that it would help them identify and write letters. They do like to pull up the balls with the magnetic pull of the pen (science, so that's good), and push them back down with their fingers, but after two minutes they lose patience and are shaking the board. Be warned this is not the best tool for learning to write letters.. there are much better and more satisfying ways children can learn that skill.

CVCBSER Flash Smooth Swing FX Dueling Lightsaber with12 Colors and 9 Kinds Mode Sounds Changeable Premium Aluminium Alloy Handle Light Saber Toys (Silver) This is my first lightsaber in about a decade. The last one I owned what a Force FX by Hasbro; my, how technology has evolved.

This lightsaber is cheaper than the one I purchase, yet has a lot more to offer. While it doesn't have the "expanding" lights (it's sort of like a flashlight), the features it has make up for it. There's only one button, yet it does so much. Initial long press wakes it up or puts it to sleep. While it's on standby, there are button sequences that control music, volume, and sound font.

With the light emitted, the lightsaber has clash functionality, and the ability to change colors. What I love about changing colors is that the colors cycle in a rainbow fashion; there is no predetermined number of colors. See a color you like between cycles? Stop on it and it stays. Pretty nice.

The smooth swing works effectively, but the sound doesn't fade away; instead, there's an abrupt stop. So if you turn the lightsaber one way, the sound follows in synchronization, but immediately stops. It sort of takes away from the effect, but I imagine lightsabers with better smooth-swing functionality have better accuracy.

One day, while charging the lightsaber after a month, the charging sound came on and kept announcing the charging state. I was a little concerned, but left it. Suddenly, the sound was rapid, then silence. I checked the lightsaber and the charging light wasn't on. I tried different outlets, but no fix. Thankfully, the lightsaber is easy to disassemble, so I checked out the battery. It seems fine, but I am awaiting a new one to make sure it's just the battery that was fried.
text_fidelity_b: CVCBSER Flash Smooth Swing FX Dueling Lightsaber with12 Colors and 9 Kinds Mode Sounds Changeable Premium Aluminium Alloy Handle Light Saber Toys (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
Never Have I Ever Parent's Edition Card Game Set | Fun Game Night Party Games for Adults | for 2+ Players | Ages 17 + i thought this would be a fun gag game. If you are in mix company (right leaning vs left leaning), I would not recommend. The basic premise of the game is that each player votes on whether they think the card is true or false, but their votes don't actually matter. The person whose turn it is reads the card out loud, makes the final decision, and follows the action on the card (whether they are right or wrong). There is an action on the card for you to perform, which usually includes drinking.

First of all, this isn't much of a game because only 1 card out of 30 is false. There is so much content from the last four years and his numerous tweets that there is enough outrageous actions for all of the cards in the game. I was hoping for some outrageous cards that were false. So, you can laugh (or cringe) about all of the things he has done, but it doesn't make it fun since there isn't much strategy. If you guess that Trump said or did the things on the card, you will be right 95% of the time.

Then, on the lower right hand corner of each card you can tell if a statement is true or false depending on whether Trump is smiling or talking. Hopefully you have good eyes because they look very similar. Also, I know it is a total gag gift, but it makes no sense that the person that actually playing is the same person that is reading the card and the answer is staring them in the face.

If you are looking for an excuse to drink while reading Trump's crazy tweets over the last 4 years, this game is for you, but I can't imagine playing this game more than once.
text_fidelity_b: Never Have I Ever Parent's Edition Card Game Set | Fun Game Night Party Games for Adults | for 2+ Players | Ages 17 +

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Juniors/4+ Jurassic World Pteranodon Escape 10756 Building Kit (84 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This summer was the year of Jurassic World! My 5 turning 6 year old is too young to watch any of the Jurassic Park movies, but that didn't stop the advertisements and displays in stores from reaching audiences far and wide including my son. He already loves Legos AND dinosaurs so this was the perfect mashup for him! We already have other Lego Juniors sets (I honestly wish they would make more).

Lego Juniors are designed for 4-7 year olds. Basically, they are the same as the other Lego kits, but the instructions are more simplistic than the other kits for older children. The Legos designs are also more simple than the Lego kits for older children. The Legos are still the same size as regular Legos, so these are not an in between Duplos and Legos. If you step on them they will hurt. In addition, the pieces are tiny enough to get lost forever.

My son is a free form builder, he does not care about the actual instructions, what he cares about is the potential for creating what is shown on the package. His Lego bin is filled with Lego kits all mixed together and he has a blast creating his own world, which is limitless. So, if you are insistent on your child following the directions to a T, then I would not recommend these for a younger child. Most boys under 6 just do not have the patience for this. Frustration sets in quick and the desire to just play take over. Stick to Duplos or just plain free build sets until about age 6 or 7 if you want to stick to the instructions. However, if you don't mind the kits getting mixed up for creative play and you child loves Legos and Dinos, then this is the set for you.

As usual, the Legos are of the same quality we had when we were kids. I would recommend getting several of the Lego tools because some of this pieces are tiny and get stuck. The only way to get them out is via the Lego Tool!
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Juniors/4+ Jurassic World Pteranodon Escape 10756 Building Kit (84 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Aori Sleeping Reborn Baby Dolls 22 Inch Lifelike Newborn Baby Girl Doll Real Life Weighted Reborn Baby Toddler with Closed Eyes Christmas Baby Doll Deer Gift Set for Kids Age 3 + PROS

1. This doll has adorable, lifelike features. Its hair and eyelashes are made of realistic-looking mohair, and it has half-moon-shaped fingernails and toenails. The head, arms, legs, hands and feet are made of smooth, soft, silicone vinyl.

2. This doll is 22 inches long, as advertised, which is the size of a typical newborn baby. For changes of clothing, you can purchase newborn or size 0-3 months clothing.

3. The arms and legs are poseable. The body is of stuffed fabric, and it is slightly weighted (4 lbs), which gives the doll a realistic feel when cuddled in the child’s arms. When completely undressed, the cloth body gives the appearance that the doll is wearing a “onesie” with short sleeves. Note: because it has a cloth body, this is not an “anatomically correct” baby doll.

4. This doll comes in an attractive gift box with the following accessories included: 1 set of clothing (a beanie hat, a shirt, and pants), 1 baby blanket, 1 plush lion toy, 1 pacifier, 1 baby bottle, 1 birth certificate.

5. The price is quite reasonable for what you get.

6. This manufacturer offers a wide selection of different types of newborn baby dolls.

CONS

1. The hair is too fragile to be combed. Though the doll comes with instructions that clearly warn against doing that, the problem is, how do you convince a very young child not to comb this particular doll’s hair when it is safe for them to comb the hair of the majority of their other dolls? If all else fails, and the child accidentally pulls out this doll’s hair while combing it, the beanie hat that comes with this doll can be used to cover its resulting baldness.

NEUTRAL

1. Similar to every other doll of this type of construction, with a stuffed, cloth body, this doll should not be immersed in water to clean it. Most especially, it should NOT be put in the washer. Here are some alternatives I have personally found useful over the years for cleaning this type of doll:

Vinyl body parts: You will need baby wipes or a thin, soft, cotton baby washcloth and a soft-bristled toothbrush or a straw brush. Moisten the washcloth with warm water (it should not be dripping wet, just damp) or use a pre-moistened baby wipe to gently cleanse the doll’s vinyl surfaces. Use a dampened (not dripping wet) toothbrush or straw brush to get inside the mouth, inside and around the ears, and between the fingers and toes.

Cloth body: Ideally, if the child can be convinced to keep this doll clothed at all times (a tricky proposition), its cloth body is less likely to get soiled. If it does get dirty, you can use this stain-removing trick to clean the cloth: squirt a teaspoon of dish soap into a bowl, add a teaspoon of hydrogen peroxide and a teaspoon of baking soda, then stir these ingredients into a paste. Insert your pointer finger inside a regular washcloth and wet the portion covering your finger. (It should not be dripping wet, just damp.) Dip the damp portion of the washcloth into the paste, then rub the paste into any existing stains on the cloth body of the doll. Most stains will rub right out, but if it is a stubborn stain, allow the paste to sit on the cloth for an hour or so. Wet another clean portion of the washcloth and gently wipe away the paste. If the paste doesn’t all come out the first try, repeat the process using another clean, damp area of the washcloth.

At first glance, she's quite plain, hard- not cuddly soft and has huge eyes with real eyelashes. The minute you put her 4 "C" batteries in (Doll does not come with batteries, you have to buy them), she comes to life with the cutest expressions, movements and baby babble speech. As the child plays with Luvabella, she does more and more. Touch her chest and hear her heart beat. Touch her feet, and she talks and calls you Mama. The baby babble will grow into words and eventually phrases. She even kisses her little Lamby toy and makes cute animal sounds. When you tickle her, she giggles and waves her arms. She plays peek-a-boo and laughs while you play with her, and eventually you'll hear her say "I see you". To have a conversation, hold her feet while speaking, she will answer back first in babble, then in words, then in phrases. Kano Harry Potter Coding Kit – Build a Wand. Learn To Code. Make Magic. This KANO HARRY POTTER CODING KIT works as advertised. It requires an app (Win10, FireOS, Android, iOS) for operation and play. (The Kano Code app for the iPad seems to work well.) The wand is fairly large--big enough to look and feel like a real magic wand.

The kit includes a booklet with instructions for assembling the wand. You insert batteries into a circuit board, put a button piece and the circuit board into a part of the wand, and close the wand with another piece. Adding the last wand piece is a bit tricky, but the finished wand looks nice and doesn’t fall apart. A button on the end of the wand opens it up for battery changes. Two sets of batteries are included.

The app allows a child to create a Kano account, but sends an email to a parent’s email address to allow the parent to set the child’s privileges. The app opens to an illustrated map of the Hogwarts campus. The map has colored spots that you tap or select to open the “challenges”.

For example, an early challenge teaches the child to change the colors on a drawing of an owl. The coding is accomplished by dragging and dropping code blocks until they click together and add the color-changing capability to the wand.

As an adult who knows almost nothing about coding, I didn’t fully understand how the coding blocks went together or how the wand was supposed to be used once a new coding feature was added. With a little more study time, I’m sure that I would have figured out how to do the coding. However, if the wand is intended for a very young child, an adult with minimal coding knowledge will probably be required to help the child get started.

The coding kit also includes a nice chart of the wand motions required to execute the spells used in the Harry Potter books and movies. This kit should keep a child busy for hours, if the child is motivated to learn to use the wand.
text_fidelity_b: Kano Harry Potter Coding Kit – Build a Wand. Learn To Code. Make Magic.

Bugs in the Kitchen - Children's Board Game, Standard, 6 - 15 years My boys have had tons of fun with this game. I like it, too.

The set up is super easy, as well as playing the game. You basically put a thick cardboard piece in place, and a couple of tubes, and you're all set. It also comes with a hexbug and 12 various colored (non-moving)bugs. Each player will get 3 of those, and the goal is to get all 3 bugs to the other side first. The hexbug moves around under the board, through the tubes, and on the playing board. While he's on the playing board, you have to stop playing, and hope that he doesn't knock your bug out of place. If he does knock your bug completely off its spot, it has to go back to the beginning(after he's went off the upper board).

The only negative is the fact that the hexbug uses a button cell battery. We don't keep those things around typically, so in order to keep this game going, we'll now have to. It's still a very fun and easy game, though.

It's labeled for 6 and up, but my 3 and 5 year old children have loved it, too, along with my 8 year old. I'm guessing the 6 and up is due to a possible choking hazard, because it's a simple game to play.
text_fidelity_b: Bugs in the Kitchen - Children's Board Game, Standard, 6 - 15 years

KINCREA Smart Robot Car Kit with ArduinoIDE Robot Kit with 4 Wheel Drive,Board,Ultrasonic Sensor, Infrared Tracking Module (No Welding Required) This is a very intricate detailed and fun car kit! The smart car is just that. It does some incredible things and any child (with the help of an adult most likely), teen, or adult will love building and driving this little vehicle around using it's remote.
There are a lot of cool things about this car kit. It says it is easy to assemble but just in case you are like we are around here you'll be happy to know it comes with detailed tutorials which include video instructions, schematic diagram and a source code. They come in handy! It has a lot of interesting parts and electronic components that would take me a while to tell you about and that I think you would do better reading up above. If I tried to explain it all it would just be a big jumbled mess.
Once it's all built the car does really fun stuff. It has two control modes. It has an infrared remote control that comes with the kit and it also has an app for your mobile phone (though only Android supported at the time of this review going up). It also uses infrared to follow lines in front of it, to avoid things in front of it, and also to follow objects. It's a really fun car.
I think almost anyone that enjoys cars and building things and all that stuff will really have fun with this. The kit is filled with the tools all the tools you need and there is no welding or anything required. It's fun, semi-easy, and so worth it when you get to play with the finished product!
text_fidelity_b: KINCREA Smart Robot Car Kit with ArduinoIDE Robot Kit with 4 Wheel Drive,Board,Ultrasonic Sensor, Infrared Tracking Module (No Welding Required)

text_fidelity_a:
Bendy and the Ink Machine - Boris Buildable Figure (202 pieces), 60 months to 180 months Ok, I do not "lego". I find it equal parts boring and frustrating, that said because I'm a parent I've had to pitch in enough times that I'm "unwilling" but competent. Which is what quickly happened with this set. Granted my kid's only 7, and this is for 14+ (which at this point I agree 100% with). I'm not going to knock a star for that, mine is young and it was a risk he wanted to take. He often does the 14+ lego sets so I figured we'd be fine. NOPE. NO SIR. NOT TODAY.

There were so many tiny pieces, like unnecessarily tiny. He made it to step 2 and couldn't make heads or tails of the instructions. I took a look and also struggled which meant he felt vindicated and took off. So, I spent the next 2 hours debating life choices and contemplating day drinking. Ugh parenting is hard sometimes.

Be very aware: This is not a lego set. The pieces do not snap together as well, or stay together as well, there are no extra pieces, and the instructions are frustrating. I'm keeping my language clean here, but imagine a much more colorful word than frustrating. "Frustrating" really doesn't do the whole experience justice.

However, Boris is built. It can be done. PERSEVERANCE PEOPLE. Kiddo however is not allowed to touch it. It will go up on his bookshelf, like super high and when ever anyone walks in he is to loudly proclaim MY MOM BUILT THAT!

....on the upside it's priced pretty cheap, so if you have any kids in your life whose parents you want to torture, send this to them as a gift. So in the end I'm giving this 3 stars. One star off for the less then stellar pieces, and another star off for the horrendous instructions.
text_fidelity_b: Bendy and the Ink Machine - Boris Buildable Figure (202 pieces), 60 months to 180 months

UNO: MOO Game Not as big of a fan as I thought I would be. . . and here’s why.

First, the description on Amazon shows that there are dogs. There are no dogs.

The sheep look like monkeys. . . and the rest of the pieces don’t look like much either. The pieces simply have a little sticker face on them and it’s hard to tell what they are supposed to be. The overall artwork could have been much better.

Packaging: This comes with a cute outer paper box. . . .but it’s nearly impossible to figure out how to get it open without tearing it completely apart! Granted, if you’re not interested in keeping the outer box, then I guess it doesn’t matter. But the best way that I found to open it is to cut the piece of tape on the left end. . . then gently “unhook” the paper pieces at the bottom and slide-out the plastic “barn”.

I do NOT recommend this for three-year-olds for two reasons. #1, I think the pieces are a Choking Hazard. #2, I really don’t think they are going to “get” the game. If you follow the instructions, I think it’s really WAY too complicated for such a young age. Granted, instead of playing the game, kids could just play with the pieces in other ways.

Finally, I think this item is WAY overpriced, at least at the current price, for a Made In China toy. If you can get it cheap, then you might want to pick it up.

Disney Princess Fashion Doll Castle, Dollhouse 3.5 feet Tall with 16 Accessories and 6 Pieces of Furniture (Amazon Exclusive) This took us about an hour to put together, and was rather frustrating to assemble. That said, I hate assembling toys like this where when you snap them into place, they are almost impossible to un-snap, so you've gotta be really 100% sure before you put things together. However, once it was built – this thing is pretty epic! My kids had an absolute blast playing with it and really loved all of the Royal, golden elements.

My only issue is that I was never able to get the swing to actually function, I think I'm probably need to use some twist ties or my glue gun to make it stay put. It will swing, but as soon as you put dolls on it, the bottom wants to fall off of the swing holders. My husband couldn't figure it out either, and neither could my eight-year-old, who is remarkably good at assembling toys.

Other than that, this has just about anything one could want in a beautiful Royal Castle, lots of exciting and elegant items, areas to conduct creative play, etc.

Two critical pieces of feedback:

First, the backside has a sticking out part right in front of the door that probably helps the castle not fall over backwards, but has the side effect of making it so that you can't push this up against the wall, which is kind of unfortunate for places with limited space.

Second, I've noticed that my kids love dollhouses and items that have a little bit more of an interactive elements such as a slide, zip line, etc. I think the nonfunctional swing was meant to do the trick, but I think if they had added a few more interactive things, this would have a little bit more appeal for kids as they get older also.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Princess Fashion Doll Castle, Dollhouse 3.5 feet Tall with 16 Accessories and 6 Pieces of Furniture (Amazon Exclusive)

Most popular animals among today's current toy trends are available. The plush material is incredibly soft and the embroidered features are incredibly cute. We were able to have Kylie the Cat join our household. Her limbs were each held into place with a plastic tab, which was not difficult to clip and remove completely.

Kylie came with a booklet that tells the origin story of the Animoodles with small written profiles and photos of each toy in the series. There are also practical safety warnings regarding the magnets used in the plush.

I had some concerns about magnets in a child's toy, but the smallest magnet I can feel through the fabric is about the size of a nickle. The stitching is solid, it would be difficult to remove the magnets. Kylie has a lemon bow stitched onto her head, the colors are very cohesive. The pupil of the eyes are buttons. I would strongly advise this toy to not be available to any child under 3 or any other children that are prone to putting random objects into their mouth or being overly destructive with their toys. The button eyes and internal magnets are simply not safe for babies, toddlers or destructive children, as it's made clear in the attached booklet.

The Animoodles Magnetic Stuffed Animal Plush would make a great gift for many children. However, Kylie was in a sealed plastic bag inside the shipping box, so this may be a gift that is better to present in a gift bag rather than wrapping unless you opt to use the shipping box. Play would be expanded with more Animoodles from the series. Additional Animoodles allow for any sort of crazy plush hybrid desired.

My favorite features of the Animoodles is the creative construction and the softness of the plush material. This would make a great addition to any plush animal collection.
text_fidelity_b: Animoodles Magnetic Hazel Sloth Stuffed Animal Plush, 7.5" , Brown

In this game, you use cards with odd artwork to get your teammates to guess a set of three out of twelve possible games. The cards go in one of the seven different sections of a three-way Venn Diagram like you used to see in school. Using the clues you're given, you attempt to identify the three chosen words that the card placer is going for.

There are some fun times to be had here, but a few problems as well. The art is meant to be odd and unusual, but a good amount of it is just plain bad - characters are off-center, objects look like they're floating in the background, etc - and the cards are hard to use because they don't actually fit inside the sections of the Venn diagram. The words are usually very descriptive, but there are also some bad word chocies in the deck like "great" or "interesting" which could literally mean anything.

Unfortunately, this is competing in a crowded market - competitive, team-based family games have been done to death, so if you want to stand out, choose a game like Codenames or Just One or So Clover or...well, there's a lot of them, and they're mostly better than this.
text_fidelity_b: Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+

text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) I'm just combining my thoughts on the various guns and products into one review, in case anyone would like to do a bit of comparing in one spot.

Darts:

The darts are kind of like a third of a straw, with a cool rubber-like tip. These tips ONLY stick to the special targets, which are on the shields(both the wearable ones and the ones that attach to the guns). There are also targets that stick to the wall. (I just taped the top of these targets, as opposed to sticking the whole thing on the wall.) We tested these out on mirrors and windows. They really don't stick to anything, but the special targets.

They're mostly bright colored, which makes it easier to find them once they've been shot. You'll have to take several time outs just to gather darts.

This company has made it perfectly clear that these darts are NOT made for little ones. I just want to reinforce that. I have an 18 month old that puts things in his mouth constantly. We found a large rock in his poo diaper. :S These are simply irresistible to him with their chewy rubber tip. He's chewed the tops off a few of them, even when we were trying to keep a close eye on him. The tops DO come off when chewed on, so these are definitely a choking hazard for little ones.

I try to teach our boys to never aim a gun at anyone, but I've been hit with a few of the darts. One hurt, but the others didn't. I think it depends on how close the gun is, and simply how the dart hits a person. In general, they don't seem to hurt too much.

Other than chewing, they seem pretty sturdy, though. They're had lots of use and bending, but they still work in the guns.

Farshot Blaster:

This is the smallest gun in this line(that we have...there seems to be a smaller "clipfire"). You pull back the top to "pump it up". It will only hold 1 dart at a time for shooting, but 2 spares fit in the bottom of the gun.

This gun is the easiest to aim, as far as target practice, and if that's what you'd like it for, I'd recommend this one. I've found it to be a great stress reliever. When the little ones are creating chaos, I can pull out this gun, tape a target to the wall, and do a little target practice.

Twisted Spinner Blaster:

This is the medium sized gun in this line. To shoot it, you pull an arm on the gun back towards yourself. The darts are loaded in the round end. It will hold 8 darts. As with all the guns, it comes with removable shields.

This one is a little harder to aim, but it's still fun.

Rapid Madness Blaster:

This is the largest gun in this line. You push and pull an arm to pump it up. The trigger is super sensitive, so it takes a couple of seconds to shoot all 20 darts that it holds. Those darts are held in a clip that slides into the side of the gun. This one is the most fun, BUT you don't get much shooting time before having to round up darts.

Bandolier:

This is an adjustable strap that you can wear across your body. It has a special target that the darts will stick to. It will also hold 12 extra darts.

Eye goggles:

These are pretty cool. As advertised, they won't fog up. They're made of a thick-like plastic/rubber, and give you "bug vision". They're also adjustable. My little ones are younger than the recommended age, but the clip kept coming off with them, and we put the goggles back together so much that I wanted to throw them away. Still, I don't think adults will have that problem, and they really are pretty cool!

Targets:

These are a little smaller than I prefer, but they do come in slightly different sizes and shapes. You get different points for different areas. The darts DO stick really well to these targets, and ONLY these targets, but if the dart hits wrong, it still won't stick. I'd say our darts stuck about half the time with the larger guns, and about 3/4th of the time with the farshot blaster. You can peel the back off and it will stick to the wall/door, but as I mentioned above, I just taped it instead. They're a fun way to create a little "battle" zone in one's room, or just simple target practice.

Overall, we've had tons of fun with these guns, and just think they're all pretty awesome.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit I am a Lego fan, but I kept that in mind as I reviewed this, not wanting it to make my review unfair.
So, lets start with the kit. The pieces do not fit together as well as Lego pieces do. That’s not a huge thing, but it’s a little annoying with some of the steps.
I have to say that the instructions are much better than Lego ones –MegaBlox devised a very clear way to show what piece to put, and where to put it. That was nice. However, they lace the style Lego shows – if this were a Lego set, it would be hollow – allowing things to go inside it – this set is solid, no room inside for anything. The feet fall off easily, which gets old fast.

Plus there are many “special” bricks that will limit the owners ability to make other things out of the set. Although, that is moot if you have a sizable MegaBlox collection already.

The finished piece is nice – a little boxy – think Minions meets Minecraft.

My issue is the price though. If you look at Lego sets (aside from brand ones like Disney and some of the collectable ones) the cost is around 10c per brick.
This set works out at almost 30cents per brick. Three times the cost of a comparably sized Lego set.
The quality does not warrant that price. Despite the added value of the Despicable Me brand. If it was rounder, more interactive, or had stronger feet I would be inclines to give it a better score

If the shortcomings don’t bother you, and your life *needs* all things “Despicable Me” then you will enjoy this.
If someone else is paying for it, you will find it a bargain.

Otherwise I would recommend you get your Despicable Me and building set fix from a better product.
text_fidelity_b: Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit

ENJBRICK Harry Castle Potter Toy Building Set,Compatible with Lego Idea Building Blocks Kit for Kids and Adults 521pcs This set consists of thirteen #1 bags for Weasley's Wizarding Wheezes (the purple and orange building), eight #2 bags for Flourish and Blotts (the green and brown building), one bag of plates, instructions, and a small sticker sheet.

The bags are not numbered individually. Trust me, open all the bags for a building. So all #1 bags or all #2 bags. You’ll need a lot of space for the pieces, but it’s less frustrating in the long run. Steps require pieces from every bag as you go. Finding the pieces for each step took the longest part of this build.

The instructions are mostly clear*, but the build experience itself is frustrating. Some pieces stay together and some do not. I spent so much time rebuilding because a section would break when I put new pieces on. For example, the window section for WWW, I had to test window pieces to see which would stay together and then stay on the building. For the upper window section, where the arms come out, I had to redo that three or four times, carefully holding the windows together.

*Step 64 has the wrong pieces, there is a sheet to show the proper pieces.

The buildings are delicate. On my Flourish and Blotts building, the bottom barely stays together, so I can’t take it off the base. The buildings are hollow inside, so you can hide items. The F&B building has a tray inside, and the WWW building has a rod to use to pop the tray out. If I popped the tray out, I’d have to put the F&B building back together. I don’t care for the hiding space, I’d prefer buildings that were more stable, especially if they’re supposed to be bookends.

Some of the stickers go over multiple pieces, one sticker on 2 or 3 pieces. The Dark Mark sticker is misspelled: DRRK MRRK.

Overall, the finished set looks good, but getting to that finished set was a somewhat frustrating experience.
